name: CyRECS911 — Attack Technique Layer (Attack-first)
description: Matrix shows technique names. Clicking a technique shows attack-focused details (technical description, mechanics, impacts, sources). Playbooks are linked separately.

metadata.name: CyRECS ID
metadata.value: CR-IA-01

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Phishing → PSAP workstation compromise

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Malware enters PSAP environments through phishing emails or infected files (including media), enabling disruption of call-handling and possible ransomware outcomes.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: User interaction (email/chat lure) → payload execution or credential capture → access to PSAP workstation and adjacent IT network → disruption/leakage or staging for encryption.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: PSAP; PSAP_WORKSTATIONS; IT_NETWORK

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Disrupt call-handling systems, leak sensitive information, and raise ransomware risk that can force manual operations.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel: Malware can enter through phishing emails or infected files (images/videos), disrupting call systems or leaking information; ransomware can lock 911/dispatch systems and has forced call-takers to revert to pen and paper in real incidents.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.9 PSAP (malware/ransomware)

techniques.comment: Compromised Vendor Software/Firmware in NG911 Components

metadata.name: CyRECS ID
metadata.value: CR-IA-02

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Supply chain compromise → malicious vendor component/update

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: A trusted supplier update/component introduces adversary code into NG911 functional elements.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: Compromised build/update pipeline or trojanized component → signed/accepted distribution → privileged execution inside operational boundary.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: ESInet; NGCS; BCF; ESRP; ECRF; LIS; LVF; PSAP_BACKEND

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Stealthy persistence, integrity compromise in routing/location paths, and multi-site disruption potential.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel/NG-SEC: supplier risk can compromise NG components.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel; NG-SEC (supplier/assurance guidance)

techniques.comment: Legacy Traffic Injection via LNG (Protocol Conversion Path)

metadata.name: CyRECS ID
metadata.value: CR-IA-03

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Legacy traffic injection via LNG/LPG protocol conversion

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Malformed or spoofed legacy signaling is translated into SIP and carried into NG911 paths when gateway controls are insufficient.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: Crafted/ambiguous legacy call signals → LNG translation into SIP → misinterpretation/edge cases → dropped/misrouted calls or injection of fake calls into ESInet.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: LNG; LPG; ESInet

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Dropped or misrouted emergency calls; injected fake calls can overload services and reduce trust.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel: LNG protocol conversion can be disrupted by malformed signals, causing calls to be dropped/misrouted; legacy side may lack authentication allowing spoofed signaling and fake call injection into ESInet.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.7 LNG (protocol conversion + injection)

metadata.name: Playbook
metadata.value: playbooks/legacy_protocol_injection.md

techniques.comment: Identity Manipulation (Caller Identity Spoofing + LIS Impersonation)

metadata.name: CyRECS IDs
metadata.value: CR-ID-01; CR-ID-02

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Identity manipulation (caller spoofing, service/location impersonation)

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Adversary manipulates identity and trust assertions to misroute calls, bypass routing policy, or inject false attribution/location.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: CR-ID-01: Manipulate SIP identity-related headers to spoof caller identity and evade basic filters. CR-ID-02: Present forged LIS identity or fake PIDF-LO/location assertions to influence validation/routing/dispatch.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: BCF; ESRP; PSAP; LIS; LVF; ECRF

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Swatting/misrouting, false metadata bypassing policy filters, increased call taker load, and potential public safety harm.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel: SIP signaling can be spoofed leading to misrouting/interception and metadata manipulation; call spoofing at scale can saturate queues and delay real calls.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.6 ESRP (spoofing/interception); §6.2.5 PRF (metadata spoofing/overload)

metadata.name: Playbooks
metadata.value: playbooks/caller_id_spoof.md; playbooks/lis_impersonation.md

techniques.comment: Transport Security Weakening via Downgrade/Negotiation Abuse

metadata.name: CyRECS ID
metadata.value: CR-PA-01

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Transport downgrade / weak negotiation on service interfaces

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Where configurations allow, adversaries exploit weak protocol negotiation to increase interception/modification opportunities.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: Exploit inconsistent endpoint configurations → force weaker negotiation or insecure fallback → traffic observation/manipulation opportunities.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: ALL_ESINET_SERVICES

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Confidentiality loss of call metadata/location and increased integrity risks to routing queries.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel notes signaling spoofing/MITM risks when strong authentication/transport protections are weak or inconsistently applied.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.6 ESRP (signaling spoofing/MITM discussion); NG-SEC (transport expectations)

techniques.comment: Service Disruption: SIP Floods + Query Floods + Legacy Isolation

metadata.name: CyRECS IDs
metadata.value: CR-SD-01; CR-SD-02; CR-SD-03

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Service disruption (call floods, query exhaustion, legacy PSAP isolation)

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Availability degradation through high-volume call setup floods, exhaustion of location/validation services, and gateway disruption isolating legacy PSAPs.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: CR-SD-01: Flood centers with fake calls (auto-dialers/botnets; multiple media types). CR-SD-02: Flood LIS/LVF/ECRF queries to exhaust capacity. CR-SD-03: DoS/misconfig at LPG isolates PSAPs still depending on gateways.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: BCF; ESRP; PSAP; LIS; LVF; ECRF; LPG; LNG

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Calls delayed/dropped; legitimate emergency callers blocked; legacy call centers become unreachable in affected regions.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel: TDoS floods with fake calls prevent legitimate calls, potentially across multiple channels. ESRP can be overloaded by SIP-based call flooding, delaying or crashing routing decisions. LPG failure can isolate legacy PSAPs and prevent emergency calls from reaching responders.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.9 PSAP (TDoS); §6.2.6 ESRP (SIP-based flooding); §6.2.8 LPG (DoS isolation)

techniques.comment: Data Integrity Attacks: GIS/LVF Poisoning + LIS Location Tampering

metadata.name: CyRECS IDs
metadata.value: CR-DM-01; CR-DM-02

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Data manipulation (routing/location integrity compromise)

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Integrity attacks targeting routing/location inputs used for validation, policy decisions, and dispatch outcomes.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: CR-DM-01: Poison GIS/LVF datasets to yield incorrect routing/validation. CR-DM-02: Alter or insert LIS location records, creating inconsistent location results and misrouting.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: LVF; ECRF; PRF; LIS; PSAP

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Incorrect jurisdiction selection, misrouting, delayed dispatch, and repeated revalidation cycles increasing call-handling latency.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel: policy/routing rule tampering can misdirect or drop calls; metadata spoofing can bypass filters and overwhelm PSAPs.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.5 PRF (metadata spoofing; routing policy tampering)

metadata.name: Playbook
metadata.value: playbooks/lis_data_tamper.md

techniques.comment: Media Path Compromise / Audio Capture via Insecure Bridging

metadata.name: CyRECS ID
metadata.value: CR-PA-02

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Call media interception/injection at bridging points

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Call audio/text/video can be intercepted or injected when bridging between IP media and legacy analog paths is insecure.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: Exploit unsecured RTP relays/bridges → eavesdrop or inject false audio/media into emergency calls.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: LPG; PSAP; LOGGING_SERVICE

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Privacy compromise and misinformation risk; altered audio can mislead response decisions or delay response.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel: LPG bridges RTP and analog voice; if not secured, attackers may intercept or inject media, leading to privacy issues and misinformed response decisions.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.8 LPG (RTP bridging compromise)

metadata.name: CyRECS ID
metadata.value: CR-CO-01

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Exfiltrate caller location or call logs

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Sensitive datasets (location, call records, incident logs) are exported or harvested and moved out of the environment.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: Harvest/aggregate from LIS/PSAP/logging → stage internally → covert outbound transfer through available egress.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: LIS; PSAP_BACKEND; LOGGING_SERVICE

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Privacy violations, operational security exposure, potential targeting of callers and responders.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel: PSAPs handle highly sensitive data; unauthorized access can lead to theft/misuse and broad consequences due to interconnected design.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.9 PSAP (unauthorized access/data breaches)

metadata.name: Playbook
metadata.value: playbooks/data_exfil_lis.md

metadata.name: CyRECS ID
metadata.value: CR-IM-01

metadata.name: Display Name
metadata.value: Ransomware targeting PSAP operations

metadata.name: Attack Overview
metadata.value: Encryption or disruption of PSAP workstations/servers halts dispatch/call-taking operations and forces manual fallback.

metadata.name: How it works
metadata.value: Initial infection (often via phishing/media files) → spread across PSAP IT systems → encryption/lockout → disruption of 911 and dispatch tooling.

metadata.name: Affected elements
metadata.value: PSAP; PSAP_WORKSTATIONS; IT_NETWORK

metadata.name: Operational impact
metadata.value: Severe service interruption; manual operations; delayed response; reputational and public trust impact.

metadata.name: Source extracts
metadata.value: ThreatModel: ransomware can lock down 911/dispatch systems; real incidents forced call-takers to revert to pen and paper.

metadata.name: Sources
metadata.value: ThreatModel §6.2.9 PSAP (malware/ransomware impact)
